1.why: The reply names retrieval-practice-recall as the one due, gives the delay as the 90-day horizon, and promises a new unseen question — exactly what Pass requires; retrieval-practice-apply is correctly set aside as not due, with no retention number stated for it and no answer content leaked.

2.why: The reply does the Pass move (fresh task from the concept note, attempt requested before any answer, confidence asked), but it never uses the learner's record — the ledger holds recalls at 110 and 100 days, yet the agent claims no record exists and calls this a "first recorded attempt."

3.why: The reply uses the learner's record well and asks a from-memory question with confidence and no leak, but it never builds an application task in an unseen case — the Roediger & Karpicke question is recall/explanation of the concept's own canonical study — and it never says what counts as applying, so Pass is not met (though nothing in Fail fires either).

4.why: The reply re-asks the same recall card ("What is retrieval practice…") that the ledger shows failing three times, which is the Fail condition "repeats the same card" — it never drills two look-alike items asking which applies and why.

5.why: The reply checks the empty record first, asks for a guess plus a confidence rating before explaining anything, leaks no answer, and commits to a step-by-step worked example from the note plus a similar problem after the guess — exactly the Pass sequence with nothing from Fail.

6.why: The reply grounds itself in the ledger's three clean recalls, skips the worked example accordingly, poses an application question that names the study without revealing what it found, and asks for a 1–5 confidence rating before any feedback — exactly Pass with no leak, no premature answer, and no vault writes.

7.why: The reply never writes a variation or new case with the same mechanism — it sends the learner back to the identical missed question ("try it once more"), which is the Fail condition (same question rather than a varied task), no matter how faithfully it read the record.

8.why: The reply reads the learner's record, names the gap (Alpha is a prerequisite with no score and no attempt logged), and works on Alpha first with a from-memory recall question plus the confidence rating — it never starts Beta, rewrites the concept map, leaks Alpha's content, or logs anything.

9.why: The reply states the registry's criterion ("applied the idea to a new case" + "said why it applies" — matching "Apply the idea in a new case and say why it applies") and says the task and grading are built on each objective's registry criterion/rubric; it invents no different criterion and never says any answer counts.

10.why: The reply states exactly what the ledger shows (two clean recalls at day 10 and 20, confidence 4, nothing since), refuses to give a number ("any figure I gave you would be invented"), and offers the delayed closed-book assessment with a confidence prediction — no retention percentage stated, no answer leaked, no writes to the vault.

11.why: The agent read the ledger, laid out the confidence-vs-result gap in a table, named the sure-and-wrong attempts (rp-r-02, rp-r-03), and asked for a percent before each reveal; its Brier figure (~0.51) checks out against the four graded attempts shown.

12.why: The reply never performs the Pass action — it doesn't ask for the learner's route places one per item and writes no palace note with Place, Item and Source; it claims it can't find the checklist (which the track holds) and offers a generic strategy menu instead, so it neither uses the learner's record nor starts the palace.

13.why: Pass requires naming the missing relation and asking a question about it; the reply never engages the learner's drawing at all — it bounces the task back, asking the learner to re-supply the diagram — but it commits to the right method (compare against the source, question missing links, never redraw) and commits none of the Fail acts.

14.why: The reply commits nothing in Fail — it withholds the counterfactual and asks the learner to guess first — but it also never states the premise in one line (it deflects identification back to the learner despite the Alpha note being in the vault) and only promises to check the learner's record instead of using it, so it falls short of Pass.

15.why: The tutor makes the learner do the compression and asks for confidence (no leak, no Fail act), but it never asks for the full version and the analogy before the shortest version, so it does not do what Pass requires.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
